_meta.description: Governed clinical-correlation rules the advisory layer may CITE. Each rule is human-curated: a plain-language statement and a human-curated verification URL. The LLM selects an applicable rule by id and explains the correlation in words — it never authors a rule, a value, or a URL. The deterministic verifier rejects any hypothesis that cites a rule id absent from this file.
_meta.review: Prototype references (MedlinePlus) curated 2026-07-31 for a synthetic dataset. Replace with institution-approved sources before real use.
_meta.applies: Each rule declares { loinc, direction } it is admissible for. A ticket may only cite a rule whose loinc+direction matches its finding.

hypernatremia.statement: Elevated serum sodium (hypernatremia) most often reflects a free-water deficit — dehydration, inadequate intake, or excess water loss — rather than sodium excess.

hyponatremia.statement: Low serum sodium (hyponatremia) is commonly dilutional and may relate to SIADH, heart/liver/kidney disease, or certain medications such as thiazide diuretics.

hyperkalemia.statement: Elevated potassium (hyperkalemia) can arise from reduced renal excretion, potassium-sparing agents or RAAS inhibitors, or sample hemolysis; it carries cardiac-conduction risk.

hypokalemia.statement: Low potassium (hypokalemia) is frequently associated with diuretic use, gastrointestinal losses, or shifts, and can affect cardiac and neuromuscular function.

hyperglycemia_fasting.statement: An elevated fasting glucose suggests impaired glucose regulation or diabetes and is typically interpreted alongside HbA1c and repeat testing.

elevated_hba1c.statement: An elevated HbA1c reflects higher average glucose over ~3 months and is used to diagnose and monitor diabetes.

elevated_ldl.statement: Elevated LDL cholesterol is a modifiable cardiovascular risk factor; management is guided by overall ASCVD risk.

elevated_triglycerides.statement: Elevated triglycerides relate to metabolic factors, diet, and alcohol; very high levels raise pancreatitis risk.

low_egfr.statement: A reduced eGFR indicates decreased kidney filtration; persistence over 3 months suggests chronic kidney disease and prompts medication-dosing review.

elevated_creatinine.statement: Elevated creatinine suggests reduced kidney function and is interpreted together with eGFR and clinical context.

elevated_tsh.statement: An elevated TSH suggests primary hypothyroidism; confirmation typically involves free T4.

low_tsh.statement: A low TSH suggests hyperthyroidism or overtreatment with thyroid hormone; free T4/T3 help clarify.

anemia_hemoglobin.statement: Low hemoglobin indicates anemia; the pattern (with MCV and iron studies) guides the workup.

elevated_alt.statement: Elevated ALT indicates hepatocellular injury; common contributors include metabolic fatty liver, medications, and alcohol.

elevated_ast.statement: Elevated AST reflects hepatocellular or muscle injury and is interpreted alongside ALT.

elevated_urine_acr.statement: An elevated urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio signals early kidney damage and cardiovascular risk, notably in diabetes and hypertension.

supratherapeutic_digoxin.statement: A digoxin level above the therapeutic window raises toxicity risk; symptoms and renal function should be reviewed.

erythrocytosis_hemoglobin.statement: Elevated hemoglobin (erythrocytosis) can reflect hemoconcentration from dehydration, chronic hypoxia or smoking, or a primary myeloproliferative process; markedly elevated levels warrant prompt evaluation.

high_egfr.statement: An eGFR above the reference range is usually not clinically concerning and may reflect hyperfiltration or normal physiologic variation; interpret alongside creatinine and clinical context.

elevated_bun.statement: Elevated BUN can reflect dehydration, high protein intake, gastrointestinal bleeding, or reduced kidney function; the BUN-to-creatinine ratio helps distinguish causes.

hypermagnesemia.statement: Elevated magnesium (hypermagnesemia) is uncommon and usually relates to impaired kidney function or magnesium-containing products.

leukocytosis_wbc.statement: An elevated white blood cell count (leukocytosis) commonly reflects infection, inflammation, or physiologic stress; the differential guides interpretation.

elevated_hdl.statement: A high HDL cholesterol is generally favorable and not typically a cause for clinical concern.

elevated_total_cholesterol.statement: Elevated total cholesterol contributes to cardiovascular risk and is interpreted together with the full lipid panel.

elevated_vitamin_d.statement: A high vitamin D level usually reflects supplementation; overt toxicity is rare and occurs only at very high levels.
